front.title: Post-Quantum Cryptographic Considerations for RATS Evidence and Attestation Results

abstract.t:
This document analyzes post-quantum cryptographic considerations for Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Evidence, Attestation Results, Endorsements, and Reference Values. It describes the distinction between post-quantum key establishment and post-quantum authentication of attestation artifacts; identifies integrity, provenance, freshness, and session-context properties that must remain independently verifiable; and provides implementation guidance for artifact sizing, bounded processing, transformation, transport, failure handling, and privacy.
The document does not define a new cryptographic algorithm, attestation token, Evidence format, transport protocol, TLS extension, or key-establishment mechanism. It relies on existing RATS architecture and data models, existing COSE and JOSE mechanisms, and protocol-specific work in the Secure Evidence and Attestation Transport (SEAT) Working Group. The intended result is a set of interoperable considerations that RATS profiles and attestation-system designers can apply when deploying post-quantum-capable attestation systems.
